Forms & inputs

Purpose: collect input with native controls, dressed in tokens. The

Purpose: collect input with native controls, dressed in tokens. The browser owns behavior (validation, pickers, keyboard, AT mappings); Squircle styles the surface and associates the messages.

The row pattern

Every field is a .sq-field: label above, control in the middle, help and error below. Labels stay close to their fields; fields stay far from each other.

<div class="sq-field">
  <label for="signup-name">Full name</label>
  <input
    class="sq-input"
    id="signup-name"
    name="name"
    type="text"
    autocomplete="name"
    aria-describedby="signup-name-help"
  />
  <p class="sq-field__help" id="signup-name-help">Shown on confirmations.</p>
</div>

Controls

MarkupNotes
<input class="sq-input" type="text | email | …">All text-like types, date, time, color, file. 48px default; --small (40px, dense rows only), --large (56px).
<textarea class="sq-input">8rem minimum, vertical resize.
<select class="sq-input"> inside <div class="sq-select">Dressed select: painted token-colored, em-scaled chevron; native popup always. .sq-select--native opts back out.
.sq-combobox + input + listTypeahead: native input with role="combobox"; list is role="listbox" (see below).
.sq-file label + input + zoneFile input presented as a drop zone (see below).
.sq-rating radio groupRadio stars: DOM order is highest-first; visual fill is left-to-right 1…n (see below).
<select class="sq-input"> (bare)Native indicator kept deliberately. First-option placeholder: <option value="" disabled selected>Choose…</option>.
.sq-check / .sq-radio label rowsNative input + themed accent-color; the padded ROW is the target. Optional .sq-check__description underneath.
.sq-switch label + input[type=checkbox] + .sq-switch__trackInput carries state in the tab order; track is presentation. 56×32px.
<input class="sq-range" type="range">Native slider, themed accent, full width. Pair with .sq-range__value + aria-live="polite" for the readout.
<fieldset class="sq-fieldset"> + <legend>Checkbox/radio groups. Borderless; legend reads as the group label.

States

  • disabled / readonly: native attributes, dimmed, not-allowed.

Never fake these with classes.

  • Invalid: aria-invalid="true" (or .sq-input--invalid — the runtime

sets both). The border widens without moving layout (padding compensates). An invalid field MUST have an associated message (below).

  • Focus: border warms to accent AND the global focus ring shows for

keyboard users. Neither is ever removed.

Required marks

<label for="f-email"
  >Email address
  <span class="sq-required-mark" aria-hidden="true">*</span>
</label>

The asterisk is decorative (required announces natively). Never rely on the mark alone: the attribute + native validation do the work.

Validation (native-first)

  1. Write constraints in HTML: required, type="email",

minlength, pattern, min/max. The browser validates.

  1. Associate every error: aria-describedby="<input-id>-error" +

<p class="sq-field__error" id="<input-id>-error"> with a message that names the fix ("Enter an address like ada@example.com"). The message text — not the red border — carries the meaning.

  1. Optional enhancement: Squircle.enhanceForm(form) moves focus to

the first invalid field on submit. It never prevents or replaces native UI. setFieldError/clearFieldError manage the aria-invalid + describedby + message wiring for custom (e.g. server-side) errors. For native errors, reveal pre-rendered messages and toggle .sq-input--invalid on invalid (capture — submit does not fire while validation blocks) and re-sync on input, as examples/forms.html demonstrates.

<form id="signup">
  <div class="sq-field">
    <label for="f-email"
      >Email address
      <span class="sq-required-mark" aria-hidden="true">*</span>
    </label>
    <input
      class="sq-input"
      id="f-email"
      name="email"
      type="email"
      required
      autocomplete="email"
      aria-describedby="f-email-help f-email-error"
    />
    <p class="sq-field__help" id="f-email-help">We never share it.</p>
    <p class="sq-field__error" id="f-email-error">
      Enter an address like ada@example.com.
    </p>
  </div>
</form>
<script>
  Squircle.enhanceForm(document.getElementById("signup"));
</script>

Pre-rendered error text (as above) suits server-rendered forms; the runtime creates the message element when it does not exist.

Switch, range, and checks: keyboard

All are native inputs: Tab reaches them, Space toggles checks/switches, arrows move radios and sliders. Nothing to wire. The switch track shows the global focus ring via :focus-visible on the (visually hidden but focusable) input.

Select, dressed

<div class="sq-field">
  <label for="order-currency">Billing currency</label>
  <div class="sq-select">
    <select class="sq-input" id="order-currency" name="currency">
      <option value="usd" selected>USD — US Dollar</option>
      <option value="eur">EUR — Euro</option>
    </select>
  </div>
</div>

The wrapper paints a chevron from tokens; the select itself stays a native <select> — the popup list, its fonts, and its zoom are the browser's, always. The chevron is em-scaled (scales with zoom) and token-colored (contrast-checked), so the classic broken-custom-chevron failure modes don't apply. multiple and size selects, and .sq-select--native, keep the browser's own indicator: that chrome is part of the control there.

Combobox

<div class="sq-field">
  <label for="cb-country">Country</label>
  <div class="sq-combobox">
    <input
      class="sq-input"
      id="cb-country"
      name="country"
      type="text"
      role="combobox"
      aria-expanded="false"
      aria-controls="cb-country-list"
      aria-autocomplete="list"
      autocomplete="off"
      data-sq-combobox
    />
    <ul
      class="sq-combobox__list"
      id="cb-country-list"
      role="listbox"
      aria-label="Countries"
      hidden
    >
      <li role="option" data-value="de">Germany</li>
      <li role="option" data-value="jp">Japan</li>
      <li class="sq-combobox__empty" hidden>No countries match.</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</div>
<script>
  Squircle.init(); // or Squircle.initComboboxes(document)
</script>

The input is the value carrier: options may carry data-value to write back a machine value (the label stays what was shown while browsing). Behavior, served by the runtime:

  • Typing opens the panel and filters options by label text

(data-sq-combobox-filter="off" keeps server-driven lists intact — the runtime then only navigates).

  • ArrowDown/ArrowUp move (wrapping); Home/End jump; PageUp/

PageDown move five; Enter commits the active option; Escape closes and restores the pre-open value; Tab closes and lets focus travel.

  • The active option is announced through aria-activedescendant

(options receive ids automatically when missing); the panel hides on outside clicks and on focus leaving the group.

Keyboard typing is native (the input does the announcing); the panel is presentation.

File upload

<label class="sq-file" data-sq-file>
  <input
    class="sq-file__input"
    id="upload-logo"
    name="logo"
    type="file"
    accept="image/*"
    multiple
  />
  <span class="sq-file__zone">
    <span class="sq-file__icon" aria-hidden="true">
      <svg
        class="sq-icon"
        viewBox="0 0 24 24"
        fill="none"
        stroke="currentColor"
        stroke-width="2"
        stroke-linecap="round"
        stroke-linejoin="round"
        focusable="false"
      >
        <path d="M12 15V4" />
        <path d="m7 8 5-5 5 5" />
        <path d="M5 20h14" />
      </svg>
    </span>
    <span class="sq-file__title">Choose files or drop them</span>
    <span class="sq-file__hint">PNG, JPEG, SVG.</span>
  </span>
</label>
<script>
  Squircle.init(); // or Squircle.initUploads(document)
</script>

The input stays a real file input (Tab reaches it; the focus ring lands on the zone). The runtime binds the label as a drop target: dragging over adds sq-file__zone--hover to the zone, dropping feeds dataTransfer.files into the input (single-file inputs keep the first file), and a change event fires — the author's handler then runs the same way it does for a picker pick. The zone also picks up sq-file__zone--filled for styling completeness. Disabled is the native attribute on the input; the zone dims through it.

Rating

<fieldset class="sq-fieldset">
  <legend>Rate your onboarding</legend>
  <div class="sq-rating">
    <label class="sq-rating__star">
      <input class="sq-rating__input" type="radio" name="rating" value="5" />
      <span class="sq-sr-only">5 stars</span>
    </label>
    <label class="sq-rating__star">
      <input class="sq-rating__input" type="radio" name="rating" value="4" />
      <span class="sq-sr-only">4 stars</span>
    </label>
    <label class="sq-rating__star">
      <input class="sq-rating__input" type="radio" name="rating" value="3" />
      <span class="sq-sr-only">3 stars</span>
    </label>
    <label class="sq-rating__star">
      <input class="sq-rating__input" type="radio" name="rating" value="2" />
      <span class="sq-sr-only">2 stars</span>
    </label>
    <label class="sq-rating__star">
      <input
        class="sq-rating__input"
        type="radio"
        name="rating"
        value="1"
        checked
      />
      <span class="sq-sr-only">1 star</span>
    </label>
  </div>
</fieldset>

Stars are painted by the CSS (token-colored mask, em-scaled); the author never draws one. Options are native radios: DOM order is highest-first so that "fill everything before the checked one" paints a left-to-right 1..n visually; each option announces its label ("5 stars"); arrows move as radios always do. Pre-select a default to communicate an existing value; leave all unchecked for no default.

Theme behavior

Surfaces, borders, placeholders, help/error text, accents, and the switch track/knob are tokens; both themes were contrast-checked including invalid and disabled states. The select chevron, rating stars, and combobox panel all follow the active theme the same way.

Customization

Override --sq-input-*, --sq-check-*, --sq-switch-* tokens, or restyle in a later stylesheet. Keep the 3rem default heights unless a documented dense context justifies small.

Common mistakes

  • Placeholder as label — labels are always visible.
  • .sq-input--invalid without a message element — color alone.
  • novalidate + an incomplete custom engine — keep native validation.
  • Custom chevrons that break zoom or contrast — the dressed select

paints from tokens and scales with text; opt out with .sq-select--native (or bare select.sq-input) when unsure.

  • Errors announced only via role="alert" on every keystroke — associate

with describedby; reserve live regions for submit summaries.

  • Fake drop zones with hashes of JS that never touch the input — the

input stays the value carrier; the runtime feeds it, it doesn't replace it.

  • Rating as clickable hearts/dots divs — the radios ARE the control;

every star is a real labeled option.

Tested limitations

  • No date-picker theming beyond the surface (picker chrome is native).
  • The combobox list has no built-in result-count live region (the active

option is announced; add one if your lists are long).

  • Combobox multi-select is out of scope for now — one selection at a

time.

  • No character counters or password-strength meters (later stages).
  • enhanceForm focuses but does not scroll custom containers — native

scrollIntoView behavior applies.

  • The dressed select cannot style the popup list (that is native

chrome, deliberately).
